_comment: Whole minor blocks run through ShardState.run_block, generated by
qkc/testdata/gen_exec_golden.py against pyquarkchain. A case is a
genesis allocation, a root chain built up alongside the shard, and
the blocks in order; each block carries the serialized block itself
and every consensus output running it produced. The allocation is
the shard's GENESIS.ALLOC, so a consumer reaches the genesis state
root by applying it and nothing else.

cases.name: devnet_chain_of_three_blocks
cases.comment: three chained blocks of in-shard transfers: each block's state root is the next one's parent, the coinbase collects the reward plus that block's fees, and the sender's nonce advances across blocks

blocks.comment: one transfer, paid for at gas price 1
two transfers from the same sender, in nonce order
an empty block still pays the coinbase reward

cases.name: devnet_xshard_deposits_received
cases.comment: a root block confirming a neighbour's minor block hands this shard two deposits; the next block consumes both and the cursor lands past them

blocks.comment: root block 1 exists only so the neighbour's header can point at a root height above this shard's genesis root height, which is what gives it permission to send
root block 2 confirms the neighbour's block, so its deposits are what this block receives before any transaction

cases.name: devnet_xshard_cursor_splits_across_blocks
cases.comment: the cross-shard allowance is one deposit wide, so a root block carrying three of them is consumed over three blocks: each block stops on the soft limit and the next resumes from the cursor the previous one published (shard_state.py:1637)

blocks.comment: first slice: one deposit, cursor stops inside the neighbour's list
second slice, resumed from the published cursor
third slice takes the last deposit; the soft limit breaks the loop on it, so the cursor stops on the deposit rather than past the root block

cases.name: devnet_root_chain_coinbase_deposit
cases.comment: every root block the cursor passes produces a deposit for its own coinbase address, credited only when that address is in this shard (shard_state.py:110-137). The first root block's coinbase is in this shard, the second's is in the neighbour, and the second still produces a zero-value deposit

cases.name: devnet_xshard_before_transactions
cases.comment: a block with both halves: the deposits are credited before the transactions run, which is what lets the sender spend what it only just received in the same block

blocks.comment: A holds nothing at the start of the block and pays for this transfer out of the deposit

cases.name: devnet_native_token_gas_real_manager
cases.comment: the real general native token manager, driven through its own interface: register QETH, propose an exchange rate of 1/30000 with a genesis-token deposit, set the refund rate to 60, then send a transaction that pays its gas in QETH at 60000 — which the contract prices at 2 (test_shard_state.py:3369)

blocks.comment: the three admin calls, in the order the contract requires: nothing can be proposed for an unregistered token
gas paid in QETH, priced by the contract: 60000 QETH per gas becomes 2 QKC per gas, and 60% of the unused gas comes back

cases.name: devnet_native_token_gas_block
cases.comment: a whole block whose transaction pays gas in QETH: the manager's sale, the refund at the rate it named and the burn of the remainder all land in the block's state root, while the coinbase map stays in the genesis token

cases.name: devnet_selfdestruct_coinbase_resurrected_by_reward
cases.comment: SELFDESTRUCT does not delete the account: del_account strips it once the message is over (messages.py:351), and the end-of-block sweep decides whether the leaf survives. Here the stripped account is the block's own coinbase, so the reward paid at the end of run_block brings it back — Ethereum's unconditional delete would drop it together with the reward

cases.name: devnet_selfdestruct_then_paid_again
cases.comment: the same rule inside one block: the account is stripped by the transaction that destroys it and brought back by the next transaction that pays it

cases.name: devnet_block_rejected_bad_nonce
cases.comment: a block carrying a transaction whose nonce is far ahead is refused whole: run_block re-validates every transaction and raises on the first failure, so nothing the block did is published

cases.name: mainnet_xshard_across_evm_switch
cases.comment: the same deposit shape on both sides of ENABLE_EVM_TIMESTAMP: before it the value is handed straight to the recipient with no receipt, at it the deposit runs as an EVM message and produces one (shard_state.py:1591, messages.py:368)

blocks.comment: pre-EVM: one second before the switch
post-EVM: the switch is a >= on the block timestamp
